java-spring.note: Existing baseline oracle. Integer PKs on every entity -- exercises the non-UUID zero-resolver diagnostic path, never the resolver-generation success path.

Real @PreAuthorize coverage on BOTH sides of the exact hasRole('X') regex: the unsupported bean-expression shape and (Todo controller) an unsupported hasAnyRole-adjacent shape, both correctly falling back to TODO_ROLE. Also surfaces a real diagnostic-accuracy gap: id fields are `String` with @GeneratedValue(strategy=GenerationType.UUID) -- UUID-*generated*, not UUID-*typed* -- so isUuidType() (a strict 'UUID'/'java.util.UUID' literal check) never recognizes them, producing the same zero-resolver note as a genuinely non-UUID PK. Verified directly against scanners/adapters/java-spring.mjs's own isUuidType(), not assumed from the repo's own README.

Modern Spring Boot 3 / Java 21 real app, MIT, actively maintained. Its package layout doesn't match either moduleOf()'s domain/<module>/ convention or the @SpringBootApplication-base-package fallback, so every real entity lands in the _unknown bucket -- confirmed real, honest _unknown bucketing on a SECOND real repo beyond spring-petclinic (D-module-attribution-base-package's own original oracle).

python-fastapi.note: Existing baseline oracle -- the official FastAPI reference template. SQLModel, single-file-per-module convention (routes and models co-located), the one shape this adapter's basename-based module attribution was built around.

Real production billing-platform backend (SQLAlchemy 2.0 Mapped[...], real OAuth2 auth, genuine UUID-addressable resources). Monorepo -- scoped to server/ (the real pyproject.toml root, one level above the polar/ package itself; an earlier scoping attempt at server/polar/ mis-detected as generic-grep). Surfaces a real, significant module-attribution gap: models live in a centralized polar/models/ package while routes live in per-feature polar/<feature>/endpoints.py files uniformly named 'endpoints', so this adapter's basename-based module attribution never unifies a feature's routes and its model into one module -- entity extraction reports zero entities for every module despite the schema being fully UUID-addressable in reality.

Real, actively-used self-hosted production app (AGPL-3.0). Extremely active development -- pinning required `bskel preflight --offline` to avoid STALE_BASE failures within minutes of pinning. Same centralized-models-vs-per-feature-routes module-attribution gap as polarsource/polar (11 real modules found, all zero entities) -- a second, independent confirmation this is a real, structural adapter limitation, not a one-repo fluke.

Strongest RBAC/multi-router oracle (casbin-style permission dependency + JWT/superuser gates), SQLAlchemy-direct. A third, independent confirmation of the same centralized-models module-attribution gap (2 real modules found, both zero entities).

typescript-express.note: Real @PrimaryGeneratedColumn("uuid") entities + real bare-identifier GET-by-id routes with literal `router` naming -- exercises real UUID-PK detection and a DIFFERENT, previously-unexercised security refusal: 'no literal select: [...] allow-list found -- resolver NOT generated' (avoiding an unintended column leak), plus the same 'static scanning cannot safely determine authorization' refusal python-fastapi's entries also show. Known, pre-existing, documented limitation also present in this same shape: app.use()-level mounts (not router.use()) drop the real path prefix.
Clean route/mount-tree extraction (textbook match for detect()/verb-extraction/mount-graph). Integer (non-UUID) PK -- endpoint-extraction diversity, not entity/UUID diversity.

8 real UUID entities extracted correctly (entity extraction doesn't depend on router-variable naming). Confirms a real, separate limitation: this adapter's endpoint-extraction gate hardcodes the literal identifier `router`, and this repo's route files use non-`router` variable names (authRoutes, productRoutes, etc.), so almost no endpoints extract despite 8 real UUID entities existing.

javascript-express.note: First real oracle this adapter has ever had (verificationBasis promoted from synthetic-only to community-sample, D-oracle-corpus-pinning). Textbook match: named Router import, bare-identifier GET-by-id, real cross-file app.use mount edge, genuinely-no-ORM (raw mysql2/promise) -- exactly the real-world shape this adapter was purpose-built for.

Polished, production-shaped real app (Swagger docs, rate limiting, JWT auth). Uses Mongoose -- structurally irrelevant to this adapter (it never inspects ORM presence, always reports resource.fetch: false), still valuable route/mount-tree diversity.
Pug/MVC-style server-rendered app, multi-router mount graph -- diversity beyond JSON-REST-API-shaped apps (this adapter is route/verb-agnostic to content type).
